page: Microsoft Azure M64pds_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the arm64 processor architecture and managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provisions 64 dedicated vCPUs alongside 1024.0 GB of system RAM, establishing a high memory allocation ratio of 16.0 GB per core. The instance includes 3780 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and supports Azure Premium Storage, though it provides no dedicated GPU accelerators and zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The hardware configuration pairs 64-bit ARM processing cores with a dense memory footprint and high-capacity direct-attached solid-state storage. By leveraging 3780 GB of local NVMe capacity, the instance handles rapid paging, tempdb workloads, and ephemeral data handling without routing all transactional I/O through networked block storage. The 1:16 core-to-memory ratio provides significant headroom for caching operations and memory-resident structures that demand minimal memory eviction under heavy concurrency.

From an infrastructure perspective, the ARM64 base architecture paired with dense memory creates an efficient compute profile for large-scale enterprise deployments, avoiding the overheads associated with overprovisioned CPU cores when memory density is the primary bottleneck. The instance is suited for massive in-memory databases such as Redis and SAP HANA scale-up scenarios, large-scale relational databases, real-time analytics engines, and high-throughput data processing pipelines requiring extensive memory caching.
description: Microsoft Azure M64pds_v4 is a memory-optimized enterprise instance built on the arm64 architecture and managed through Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs and 1024.0 GB of system RAM, delivering an expansive 16.0 GB of memory per core. Local storage is provided through a high-capacity 3780 GB NVMe SSD array, supporting high-throughput ephemeral caching alongside compatibility with Azure Premium Storage volumes. The server contains no integrated GPUs and includes no complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The ARM-based compute architecture offers an efficient scaling profile for applications that are bound primarily by memory capacity rather than raw x86 instruction-set features. Because of its large memory footprint and fast NVMe scratch storage, the M64pds_v4 is well suited for hosting in-memory databases, enterprise caching layers, large relational database engines, and memory-intensive analytics pipelines.
